transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. What brings you in to see me today?

Well, doc, I guess what brings me in is... I just constantly feel like I’ve got this motor humming under my skin. Like, right under the surface, you know? Especially whenever I’m supposed to just sit still. We have these staff meetings at the building I clean, and... actually, speaking of the building, they just decided to replace all the baseboards on the second floor, which is a nightmare for me because the contractors leave dust absolutely everywhere. I mean, fine white dust all over the tile I just spent three hours buffing. I was telling my supervisor that if they're going to do construction, they need to seal off the vents, but nobody listens to the janitor, right? 

But anyway, yeah, in those staff meetings, or like at church event briefings, I just can't do it. I end up shifting in my seat the whole time, or I just stand up in the back, or I have to find some excuse to go check the trash bins or something just to move around. It's driving me a bit crazy.
Do you have trouble paying attention or following through on instructions?

Paying attention? No, I don't think so. I mean, if someone gives me a job, I get it done. I don't have trouble following instructions. Like, my supervisor gives me a checklist every night. Usually it's the standard stuff, but last week he had me strip the wax in the north corridor. Which, let me tell you, is a huge pain because management just switched to this new eco-friendly floor stripper. It's supposed to be better for the environment, I guess, but it takes twice as long to eat through the old wax. And the smell is just... it’s like sour apples and vinegar. 

My wife absolutely hates it. She actually made me start leaving my work boots out on the back porch because of the smell. Which reminds me, I really need to fix the screen door out there, the hinges are completely rusted through from all the rain we got last spring. We had that huge storm, remember? Knocked out power in our neighborhood for two whole days. We had to eat everything in the freezer so it wouldn't go bad. 

But, uh... wait, what did you ask me? Oh, right, instructions. No, no problem there. I do what I'm told and I get my work finished. It's really just the sitting still and the meetings that I can't handle.
Do you often act on impulse without thinking things through?

Act on impulse? I don't really think so. I mean, I'm not going out and buying sports cars or anything like that. Although, my neighbor, Frank, he just bought this vintage Corvette. Beautiful car, cherry red, but he keeps parking it halfway over my property line. I've told him three times already, "Frank, you gotta keep it on your side," but he just laughs it off. He's always been like that, even when we were coaching Little League together back when the kids were small. My son played shortstop, and Frank’s boy was the pitcher. Kid had a cannon for an arm, but he couldn't hit the broad side of a barn. We made it all the way to the state semi-finals that year, though. We had this big pizza party at Shakey's to celebrate. Man, I haven't been to a Shakey's in years. Do they even still have those around? I think the one on 4th Street turned into a dry cleaner. 

But, uh, no. I wouldn't say I do things without thinking. I'm a pretty regular guy, you know? Just trying to get through the day without crawling out of my skin.
Do you often find yourself fidgeting or feeling restless when you're not at work?

Yeah, it’s not just at work. Even when I’m trying to relax, it happens. Like, my wife and I will go fishing, or she drags me to bingo on Thursday nights, and I just can't sit there quietly. I always catch myself tapping my foot, or talking way too loud, or constantly messing with my tackle box or my bingo pencil. 

Speaking of the tackle box, I actually just bought this new one from Bass Pro. It’s got these modular compartments, which is an absolute lifesaver because I used to always get my spinnerbaits completely tangled up with my crankbaits. Have you ever tried getting a treble hook untangled from a rubber worm? It’s a total nightmare. Anyway, my wife caught this huge largemouth bass last weekend, must have been four pounds. She was so proud, she actually wanted to get it mounted, but I told her taxidermy prices have gone through the roof. My buddy Jim had a buck mounted last fall and it cost him an arm and a leg, plus the guy took six months to finish it. He had his shop over on Route 9, but I think they're tearing that whole strip mall down to build condos. Everything's condos these days, you know? There's no open space left. 

But, uh... yeah, so even doing that stuff, fishing or bingo, I just get so fidgety. It gets really hard for me to just be quiet and actually enjoy the downtime like she does.
Do you often have mood swings?

Mood swings? No, I don't think so. I mean, I get a little grumpy if I skip lunch, but who doesn't, right? Like last Tuesday, I didn't get to eat because the main cafeteria at the building was totally shut down for an emergency clean. A water pipe burst right over the prep stations. What an absolute mess. The emergency plumbers they called in must have charged a fortune for a rush job like that. 

I used to know a plumber, Gary, who would've fixed it for half the price. He drove this beat-up old Ford Econoline van that was always breaking down on him. We spent an entire Saturday once just trying to swap out the alternator in his driveway. His wife brought us out some iced tea while we were working, and man, it was the best sweet tea I’ve ever had. She was from somewhere down South, Georgia maybe? They put peaches in everything down there. I love a good peach cobbler. My grandma used to make one every Fourth of July, and we'd eat it out on the porch watching the fireworks over the lake. They don't do the lake fireworks anymore, though, because of the fire hazard with the dry brush. 

But, uh... wait, what was the question? Oh, mood swings. Yeah, no, I'm pretty even-keeled. Just a regular guy. Nothing like that.
Do you often find yourself talking more than others in social situations?

Talk more than others? I guess maybe sometimes, but mostly I just like a good conversation. You know, you get to talking with folks and one thing leads to another. Like the other day, I was down in the basement of the building, just emptying out the recycling bins, and the new security guard, Marcus, was down there. Nice kid, just out of the military. He was telling me about this deployment he had in Germany, and it got me thinking about my uncle who was stationed there back in the seventies. 

My uncle brought back this amazing cuckoo clock from the Black Forest. Real intricate wood carving, little dancers that came out on the hour. He gave it to my mom, and she kept it in the hallway for years. The ticking used to drive my dad absolutely crazy, though. He was a light sleeper. He worked the night shift at the bottling plant, so he had to sleep during the day. That plant closed down, what, fifteen years ago now? They turned the whole lot into one of those fancy outdoor shopping centers. The ones with the brick walkways and the overpriced coffee shops. I went in there once to get a cappuccino and it cost me seven bucks. Seven bucks for a cup of coffee! And the cup wasn't even that big. 

But, uh, talking too much... I don't know if I talk more than anyone else. I just have a lot of stories, I guess. People seem to listen, mostly. Or they nod, anyway.
Are your difficulties with sitting still and fidgeting causing problems for you at home or with your family?

Well, at home my wife mostly just rolls her eyes, but it's actually at work where it's turning into a real headache. I've been getting a lot of complaints lately, and my supervisor is constantly correcting me. He says I'm always missing parts of his instructions, and apparently, I'm creating a lot of friction during the room turnovers and when we have to make supply decisions. It got to the point where he actually pushed me toward the employee assistance program. 

Speaking of supply decisions, you wouldn't believe the new floor wax corporate is making us use. It smells terrible, like industrial pine mixed with cheap cologne. We used to use this citrus stuff that was so much better. The guy who used to order our supplies, Frank, he actually cared about that stuff. He retired to Florida last year, bought a little place down in Boca. I went to Florida once back in '98, took the kids to Disney World. Man, the lines were just incredible. We waited two hours just to get on Space Mountain, and then the ride broke down right when we got to the very front! My youngest started crying, and he dropped his Mickey Mouse ice cream bar right on the hot pavement. Those ice cream bars were a total rip-off, too. I think they were like five bucks back then, I can't even imagine what they charge now.

But, uh... wait, what did you ask me? Oh, right, if it's causing problems. Yeah, so my supervisor wants me doing this EAP thing because of the friction with the turnovers and all that.
Do you think your main problem is that you can't sit still or that you have trouble focusing on what's going on around you?

Well, I think it's the sitting still part. What brings me in is I feel like I've got a motor humming under my skin whenever I'm supposed to sit still. Like, when we have those staff meetings, or even at church event briefings. I just end up shifting around, standing up, or finding some excuse to move, you know? 

Speaking of church, they're redoing the whole basement right now. Tearing up the old carpet and putting down tile. They asked me for some advice on what kind of grout to use, since I deal with that stuff all the time at work. I told them to go with a dark gray, because white grout is just a nightmare to keep clean. You get one spill of fruit punch down there during Sunday school, and it's stained forever. We had this red punch when I was a kid at vacation bible school, and I swear it tasted like pure sugar and red dye. My mom wouldn't let us drink it at home. She was always on this health kick, making us eat carob instead of chocolate. Have you ever had carob? It is not the same. It tastes like dirt. She used to make these carob chip cookies and try to pass them off as chocolate chip. My brother and I would just feed them to the dog when she wasn't looking. Poor Buster, he didn't know any better. He was a good dog, though. A golden retriever mix. We found him wandering around the old drive-in theater that used to be on Route 9. 

But, uh, what were we talking about? Oh, right, the sitting still. Yeah, it's like a motor running inside me. I just can't stay put during those meetings.
Do you think you would have trouble sitting still even if you were doing something you really enjoyed?

Well, yeah, I guess so. Even when I’m trying to relax, like when I go fishing with my wife. You'd think fishing would be relaxing, right? But I catch myself tapping my foot on the boat, or talking too loud, or just messing with my tackle box constantly. I can't just sit there and watch the bobber. My wife loves it, though. She grew up on a lake up in Michigan. Her dad had this little aluminum rowboat, real old thing, probably from the fifties. They used to go out at dawn to catch crappie. 

I've never been a morning person myself. Working the late shifts cleaning the building, you get used to being up when everyone else is asleep. The building is so quiet at 2 AM. Sometimes the only sound is the hum of the vending machines in the breakroom. They put in one of those new machines that takes credit cards, but it's always breaking down. Last week, it ate a guy's dollar and he got so mad he kicked the glass. Didn't break it, but left a big scuff mark I had to buff out. Buffing those floors is an art, really. You gotta use the right pad on the machine, or you'll strip the finish right off. 

But, uh, what was the question? Oh, doing things I enjoy. Yeah, even at bingo night. I'm tapping my pencil, shifting around... it gets hard for me to just be quiet and enjoy it.
Do you think you would be able to focus on a task if you were allowed to get up and move around while doing it?

You know, I'm really not sure if that would help or not. I mean, my whole job is moving around, right? Pushing the cart, doing the floors... 

Speaking of the cart, they finally replaced the casters on mine last week. I had this one wheel that squeaked so loud it sounded like a dying bird echoing down the empty hallways. I kept telling the maintenance guy, "Just give me a can of WD-40, I'll take care of it," but he said they had to order a whole new set of wheels because of some new vendor contract corporate signed. It took three weeks! Everything takes forever with these new contracts. 

It's exactly like when I tried to get a permit to expand my back deck at home. The city made me jump through so many hoops. I wanted to use this composite decking—you know, the stuff that doesn't rot or fade? It's a lot more expensive up front, but you never have to stain it. My brother-in-law used regular treated pine on his deck, and within three years it was warping and giving everyone splinters. He had this big 4th of July barbecue a couple years ago, and my nephew got a splinter the size of a toothpick right in his big toe. Screamed bloody murder. We had to hold the poor kid down while my sister dug it out with a pair of tweezers. She's got a strong stomach for that kind of thing, she used to be a dental hygienist before they moved out to Ohio. 

But, uh... wait, what was the question? Oh, focusing if I can move around. Yeah, I don't really know. I've never really thought about it since I'm always on my feet anyway.
Do you think your difficulty with sitting still is more related to not being able to focus or because you feel an internal restlessness?

Well, it really feels like that restlessness, you know? It's just this constant need to be doing something. Like, on my shifts, I'll go straight from mopping the lobby to checking the trash cans, and then I'm off straightening the chairs in the conference rooms without even taking a breath or stopping. And even when I get home, instead of just sitting down on the couch after a long night, I'll head out to the garage and start puttering around, maybe re-sorting my tools or something. 

I've got this huge pegboard out there for all my tools. I spent a whole weekend outlining every single wrench and hammer with a black marker so I'd know exactly where they go. My neighbor, Dave, saw me doing it and thought I was crazy. He keeps all his tools thrown into this one rusty metal toolbox he got at a garage sale. I don't know how he ever finds anything in there. He borrowed my socket set once to fix his lawnmower—one of those old riding ones with the engine in the back—and he brought it back missing the 10-millimeter socket. It's always the 10-millimeter, isn't it? I swear those things just vanish into thin air. I had to go to the hardware store just to buy a replacement, and they sell them individually now just because people lose them so much. The guy at the hardware store, Frank, he's been working there since I was in high school. He knows where every single screw and bolt is in that place. 

But, uh... what were you asking? Oh, right, the restlessness. Yeah, it's definitely that internal feeling. I just can't seem to stop moving, whether I'm at work or at home.
Do you think you would be able to pay attention to a task if it was really interesting to you, or would you still find your mind wandering?

I honestly couldn't tell you. I've never really paid attention to whether my mind wanders more or less when I actually like what I'm doing. 

Like, I really enjoy watching those history documentaries on PBS. The ones about big engineering projects? They had this one on the Hoover Dam a few weeks ago. Fascinating stuff. Did you know they had to run hundreds of miles of pipes through the concrete and pump ice water through them just to cool it down? The narrator said otherwise it would have taken a hundred years for the concrete to cure. A hundred years! I actually went out to see it back in '98. Me and the wife took a trip to Vegas for our anniversary. We didn't gamble much, though. The casinos are just too loud, all those bells and flashing lights, and the cigarette smoke gets right in your eyes. But the buffets, oh man. We went to this one at the Excalibur, and they had a carving station with prime rib that was just out of this world. The guy slicing it had this massive knife, looked almost like a sword, which I guess fits the whole medieval castle theme they got going on there. He was telling me he used to be a butcher up in Chicago before he moved out to the desert for his arthritis. Said the dry heat works wonders for his joints. 

But, uh... I'm sorry, what were we talking about? Oh, right, paying attention to interesting things. Yeah, I really don't know. Even with those documentaries I like so much, I'm usually getting up to fix a snack or fiddling with something on the coffee table while they're on, so I couldn't say for sure.
Do you think you would be able to sit still if you were doing something that required your full attention?

Well, honestly, probably not. Even if I'm supposed to be giving something my full attention, it's like... I feel like I've got this motor humming right under my skin whenever I'm expected to just sit there. Like in those monthly staff meetings, or when I'm at the church helping out with event briefings. I just end up shifting in my seat, standing up in the back, or finding some excuse to go check on something. 

Speaking of the church, they're doing this massive renovation on the fellowship hall right now. Tearing up all the old linoleum and putting down that luxury vinyl plank stuff. It's supposed to look like real hardwood, but it's waterproof. Which is smart, because you wouldn't believe how many times the youth group has spilled red bug juice on that floor. I remember one time, Pastor Dave's youngest kid—he's a real handful, that one—knocked over an entire cooler of it during vacation bible school. It looked like a crime scene in there. We tried everything to get the stain out. Bleach, baking soda, even this industrial degreaser I brought from work. Nothing touched it. My wife ended up having to put a big area rug over it just so the Ladies Auxiliary wouldn't complain during their Wednesday morning prayer breakfast. They're real particular about how that room looks. Mrs. Higgins, she's the head of the committee, she even measures the distance between the chairs... 

Wait, what did you ask me? Oh, sitting still. Yeah, no, even if I need to pay attention, that motor feeling just keeps me moving around.
Do you think your mind wanders because you're bored or because you just can't seem to focus on one thing?

I honestly couldn't say. I've never really stopped to figure out if it's because I'm bored or if I just can't lock onto one thing. 

Like, when I'm running the floor buffer at work... you'd think that's a boring job, right? Just back and forth down the exact same hallway. We use this heavy-duty Clarke machine. The cord on it is massive, bright yellow, gotta be fifty feet long at least. My buddy Gary, who works the day shift, he actually ran over the cord with it last month. Tripped the main breaker for the whole east wing. It was a total mess because the accounting firm on that floor was right in the middle of tax season. They had all these temps working late, eating takeout right at their desks. You wouldn't believe the sheer volume of trash I have to haul out of there in April. Mostly Chinese food cartons and pizza boxes. One guy actually left a half-eaten container of egg foo young in his wastebasket over a three-day weekend, and the smell... man. I had to use industrial deodorizer just to make the cubicle livable again. The office manager, Susan, she was furious. She's always leaving these passive-aggressive sticky notes on the microwave in the breakroom about cleaning up splatters anyway, so you can imagine how she reacted to the smell of rotting eggs. She buys those expensive gel pens, the ones that write in purple ink, just to write the notes... 

But, uh... sorry, what was the question again? Oh, right, the mind wandering thing. Yeah, I really don't know why it happens, to be honest with you.
Do you think your mind wanders off because you're having trouble paying attention or because you're just too restless to sit still?

I couldn't really tell you which one it is, to be honest. It's hard to separate the two. Like, am I restless or just not paying attention? I really don't know. 

I do know that sitting still is tough, though. Like in our breakroom down in the basement at work. They just swapped out all our old chairs for these new ergonomic ones. The building manager said they're supposed to be better for your lumbar. But they have these caster wheels that just roll if you even breathe too hard. It's like trying to sit on a skateboard. Reminds me of this shopping cart I got stuck with at Home Depot last weekend. One wheel was completely locked up, just dragging across the concrete. I was in there looking for some weather stripping because the seal around my back door is completely shot. Every time it rains, water pools right on the mudroom floor. And it's been pouring lately, hasn't it? Just buckets. My neighbor, Frank, his gutters actually overflowed and washed out his wife's entire hydrangea bed. She was out there in a yellow poncho trying to save the roots with a trowel. Looked miserable. Frank wouldn't go out to help her, though. He's terrified of lightning ever since a tree got struck near his golf cart back in the 80s... 

Wait, I'm sorry, I lost the thread again. What did you ask me? Oh, right, being restless or having trouble paying attention. Yeah, I really couldn't say which one is the main culprit. I've never really been able to figure that out.
Do you think you would have trouble following instructions if you were doing something that really interested you?

Well, I don't know, honestly. I've never really thought about it. Even if it's something I like, I'm not sure if I'd have trouble following the steps or not. 

Like when I'm restoring those old antique radios in my garage. I love doing that. I've got this beautiful 1938 Zenith console I'm working on right now. The veneer was completely peeling off when I found it at this estate sale out in the county. The guy running the sale, he had on this ridiculous straw hat, kept trying to upsell me on a box of rusty spark plugs. I don't even know what I'd do with spark plugs, I drive a Honda Civic. It's got over two hundred thousand miles on it, though. Still runs like a top, mostly because I change the oil every three thousand miles on the dot. My brother-in-law, Gary—different Gary from work—he never changes his oil. He just tops it off when the light comes on. I keep telling him he's going to ruin the engine block on that Ford Ranger of his. And those parts aren't cheap anymore. You go down to the AutoZone now, and the guys behind the counter don't even know what a carburetor is. They just stare at their computers. Everything's computerized now, isn't it? Even the new floor scrubbers we got at work have these digital readouts. 

Sorry, what were we talking about? Following instructions? Yeah, I don't really know if I'd have trouble or not, even if I was really into whatever I was doing. I just haven't noticed one way or the other.
Do you think you would be able to sit still and focus if you were doing a task that you found extremely interesting and engaging?

Well, you know, even if it's something I really enjoy, I still have a hard time just... being still and quiet with it. Like when I go fishing with my wife. I love fishing, always have. But I'm out there on the boat, and I catch myself tapping my foot against the aluminum hull, or I'm constantly reorganizing my tackle box, switching out lures I haven't even used yet. Or I start talking too loud, and my wife has to shush me because I'm scaring the bass. She's got this old fiberglass rod her dad gave her, must be from the seventies. The cork handle is all worn down. Her dad was a real character, used to run a hardware store out in the valley before the big box places ran him out. He sold these custom birdhouses he made out of scrap lumber. People would come from two towns over just to buy them. He painted them these bright, garish colors—neon green, hot pink. Said the birds liked it, but I think he was just using up whatever clearance paint he had in the back room. They had this one paint mixer back there that sounded like a jet engine taking off every time he turned it on. You had to yell just to hear yourself think...

Wait, sorry, what was I saying? Oh, right, sitting still. Yeah, even when I'm trying to relax, like at fishing or when we go to bingo at the lodge, I'm always messing with my pencil or tapping the table. It's just hard for me to be quiet and enjoy the moment, even when I want to.
Do you think your difficulty with sitting still is more because you can't focus on what's being said or because you feel an overwhelming need to move?

Honestly, I think it's just this... this overwhelming need to keep moving. I don't really have an off switch. Like on my shifts at the building, I’ll go straight from mopping the floors to checking the trash cans to straightening out the chairs in the conference rooms without really stopping to take a breath. I just keep going. 

And those conference room chairs, they're those heavy leather ones with the metal armrests. The executives leave them scattered everywhere like toddlers. And don't even get me started on the trash. The purchasing department just switched us to these new biodegradable bags to be more "green," right? But they tear if you even look at them wrong. I had a bag split wide open on me Tuesday—someone dumped a whole cup of half-drank iced coffee in there, and it went all over my work boots. They’re my good leather boots, too. I had to hose them off in the driveway the second I got home. 

But see, even then, after a long shift on my feet, I don't just go inside and sit down on the couch. I’ll go straight into the garage and start puttering around. I’ll spend two hours re-sorting my tools or reorganizing my socket sets instead of just resting after work. I’ve got this big pegboard my dad gave me, must be forty years old. The hooks are all rusted, but I can't bring myself to throw it out. He used to keep his workbench so clean you could eat off it. He always said a man's tools tell you everything you need to know about his character. He had this one vintage ball-peen hammer that he found at a flea market back in... 

Wait, I'm doing it again, aren't I? I completely lost track. What did you ask me about sitting still?
Do you feel like you're moving around because you're restless inside or because something outside is distracting you?

Well, it's definitely from the inside. It's not like a bird flies by the window and I have to get up. It's more like... I feel like I've got this motor humming right under my skin, you know? Especially when I'm supposed to just sit there, like during those staff meetings at work or the briefings we have before church events. I just can't take it. I end up shifting around in my chair, or I have to stand up, or I'll just make up some excuse to go check on something just so I can move. 

Those church events, though, they're getting out of hand. Last week they had this potluck for the spring festival, and the woman organizing it—Mrs. Higgins—she insisted on having everything color-coordinated. Even the napkins had to match the potato salad bowls. I don't know where she finds the time. Her husband, Tom, he just retired from the post office after thirty years. Good pension, I hear. He bought this massive RV, one of those Class A motorhomes that looks like a tour bus. He parked it in his driveway and it took up the whole thing, blocking the sidewalk. The homeowners association threw an absolute fit. They sent him three letters before he finally moved it to a storage lot out by the highway. That storage lot used to be a drive-in theater when I was a kid. We used to sneak in by hiding in the trunk of my buddy Dave's Chevy Nova. Dave was a wild one, he actually joined the Navy and ended up stationed in... 

Sorry, I'm rambling again. But yeah, to answer your question, it's definitely an inside restless feeling, like a motor that just won't shut off.
Do you think your main issue is that you can't pay attention or that you just can't sit still?

Well, I don't really know if I can separate the two, honestly. I mean, I guess it's both? Or maybe one causes the other? I'm not really sure. But I do know that the sitting still part is a huge problem. Like, if I'm forced to sit still, my brain just goes a million miles an hour, and I can't pay attention anyway. 

It’s like when I try to watch a movie with my wife. She loves those historical dramas, the ones with the big dresses and everyone talking in those stiff British accents. We tried to watch one last weekend—something about a queen, I don't know. It was three hours long. Three hours! Who makes a movie that long? The director, I read somewhere, he’s known for doing these massive epics. He actually filmed a lot of it on location at this real castle in Scotland. I saw a documentary about that castle once. They have this huge problem with dampness in the stone walls, which makes sense, it's Scotland, it rains all the time. But they have to hire these specialized stonemasons to come in and repair the mortar using traditional techniques. You can't just use modern cement, it ruins the stone. It traps the moisture inside and the whole thing just crumbles from the inside out. My buddy Gary, he used to do masonry work before he hurt his back. Fell off a scaffolding on a commercial job downtown. The company tried to fight his worker's comp claim, said he wasn't wearing his harness right. Can you believe that? Gary’s the most careful guy I know. He sued them, of course, and ended up getting a decent settlement, bought a little cabin up by the lake...

Wait, sorry. What were we talking about? Oh, right, paying attention versus sitting still. Yeah, I don't know which is the main issue, to be honest. I just know I can't really do either one very well.

doctor.intent: determine if the patient's symptoms are associated with inattention
doctor.question: Do you have trouble paying attention or following through on instructions?

target_item.reason: The doctor is asking about inattention symptoms (trouble paying attention or following through on instructions), which are part of the Inattentive presentation. doctor.question: Do you feel like you're moving around because you're restless inside or because something outside is distracting you?

target_item.name: Feeling_Restless
target_item.manifestation: What brings me in is I feel like I’ve got a motor humming under my skin whenever I’m supposed to sit still, like in staff meetings or church event briefings, and I end up shifting, standing, or finding some excuse to move around.
target_item.reason: The doctor is asking about the internal feeling of restlessness versus external distraction, which directly maps to the symptom of feeling restless (S012).

patient.answer:
Well, it's definitely from the inside. It's not like a bird flies by the window and I have to get up. It's more like... I feel like I've got this motor humming right under my skin, you know? Especially when I'm supposed to just sit there, like during those staff meetings at work or the briefings we have before church events. I just can't take it. I end up shifting around in my chair, or I have to stand up, or I'll just make up some excuse to go check on something just so I can move. 

Those church events, though, they're getting out of hand. Last week they had this potluck for the spring festival, and the woman organizing it—Mrs. Higgins—she insisted on having everything color-coordinated. Even the napkins had to match the potato salad bowls. I don't know where she finds the time. Her husband, Tom, he just retired from the post office after thirty years. Good pension, I hear. He bought this massive RV, one of those Class A motorhomes that looks like a tour bus. He parked it in his driveway and it took up the whole thing, blocking the sidewalk. The homeowners association threw an absolute fit. They sent him three letters before he finally moved it to a storage lot out by the highway. That storage lot used to be a drive-in theater when I was a kid. We used to sneak in by hiding in the trunk of my buddy Dave's Chevy Nova. Dave was a wild one, he actually joined the Navy and ended up stationed in... 

Sorry, I'm rambling again. But yeah, to answer your question, it's definitely an inside restless feeling, like a motor that just won't shut off.

doctor.intent: Determine if the patient's symptoms are primarily due to attention deficit or hyperactivity
doctor.question: Do you think your main issue is that you can't pay attention or that you just can't sit still?

target_item.reason: The doctor is asking a conceptual diagnostic question comparing inattention with hyperactivity/inability to sit still, which does not map to a specific new symptom in the patient's profile.

patient.answer:
Well, I don't really know if I can separate the two, honestly. I mean, I guess it's both? Or maybe one causes the other? I'm not really sure. But I do know that the sitting still part is a huge problem. Like, if I'm forced to sit still, my brain just goes a million miles an hour, and I can't pay attention anyway. 

It’s like when I try to watch a movie with my wife. She loves those historical dramas, the ones with the big dresses and everyone talking in those stiff British accents. We tried to watch one last weekend—something about a queen, I don't know. It was three hours long. Three hours! Who makes a movie that long? The director, I read somewhere, he’s known for doing these massive epics. He actually filmed a lot of it on location at this real castle in Scotland. I saw a documentary about that castle once. They have this huge problem with dampness in the stone walls, which makes sense, it's Scotland, it rains all the time. But they have to hire these specialized stonemasons to come in and repair the mortar using traditional techniques. You can't just use modern cement, it ruins the stone. It traps the moisture inside and the whole thing just crumbles from the inside out. My buddy Gary, he used to do masonry work before he hurt his back. Fell off a scaffolding on a commercial job downtown. The company tried to fight his worker's comp claim, said he wasn't wearing his harness right. Can you believe that? Gary’s the most careful guy I know. He sued them, of course, and ended up getting a decent settlement, bought a little cabin up by the lake...

Wait, sorry. What were we talking about? Oh, right, paying attention versus sitting still. Yeah, I don't know which is the main issue, to be honest. I just know I can't really do either one very well.
